title: Localizing a flat module over an algebra
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $M$ be an $A$-module that is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $A$. Regard $S^{-1}M$ as an $R$-module through the localization map $A\to S^{-1}A$. Then $S^{-1}M$ is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.39.18, Tag 00HT, part (6), localization argument

proof.text: Use Module.Flat.iff_lTensor_injectiveₛ. For a submodule N of an R-module P, flatness of M gives injectivity of N.subtype.lTensor M. Regard this as the A-linear map AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor A M N.subtype. The map LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M is an A-localization, and IsLocalizedModule.rTensor supplies localization structures on the tensor maps. IsLocalizedModule.map_injective therefore gives injectivity of the localized tensor map; IsLocalizedModule.map_lTensor identifies it with AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor A (LocalizedModule S M) N.subtype, whose underlying R-linear map is the required tensor map.
